description: Mathematics: WIT structural checking, Lean/Mathlib kernel verification, and bounded computational search. The baseline domain — the frame was factored out of a system built for exactly this field, so this pack is the reference instantiation of all five contract items.

artifact_kinds: structured proof sketch in the field's own notation
bounded search harness plus a re-verified witness
examples: Prove that for every integer n, the sum of the first n odd numbers equals n squared.
Show that there is no largest prime, or give a counterexample if the claim fails.
Formalize the statement that a continuous function on a closed interval attains its maximum.
Determine whether every graph whose vertices number n and whose edges exceed n^2/4 contains a triangle.
Prove or disprove: the sequence defined by a(n+1) = a(n)/2 + 1/a(n) converges for every positive start.
Find a tight upper bound for the least n with this combinatorial property, and confirm it by exhaustive search over the stated finite range.
For all propositions P and Q, if P implies Q and P holds, then Q holds.
counter_examples: Prove that the gene knockout reduces protein levels in the clinical trial cohort.
Show that conversion improved: the p-value is below 0.05 across the market share test.
Check that the retry counter never exceeds its configured upper bound in production.
Summarise what the focus group said about pricing and recommend a change.

corpus.description: Mathlib declaration retrieval: exact formal type, module, import list, dependency list, aliases. Returns known premises vs. search targets, and never assumes a premise exists. An empty result is information, not a reason to fall back to a guess.

tiers.name: structural
tiers.description: WIT structural check: one MODULE, labels sequential within scope, every step carries a keyword and a BY justification, every bracketed reference resolves, no forward references, no cross-CASE references, QED present. Catches shape errors before any expensive semantic work.
tiers.contamination_controls: Parses only the artifact; has no access to the expected conclusion and cannot be tuned toward one.

tiers.name: kernel
tiers.description: Lean elaboration against Mathlib. A candidate either type-checks or it does not, and no argument changes that. Feedback order: `lake env lean <file>` as the default and the floor, then a full `lake build` for final confirmation only. There is no per-command fast path — see prefix_reuse below and doctrine/kernel_economics.md. WITSOC2_LEAN_PROJECT must point at a built Lean project, or the tier elaborates against the ambient toolchain with an empty search path and every library import fails.
tiers.two_sided_evidence: scripts/negative_control/ holds four known-bad artifacts — a placeholder escape, a weakened target, a hidden binder assumption, and a type error. The tier must reject all four; scripts/check.py --self-test runs them.
tiers.contamination_controls: The kernel is upstream software with no knowledge of this run. The frozen target hash is computed before elaboration and re-checked after, so the statement cannot be edited to fit the argument.

prefix_reuse.measured_value: Import elaboration is 98% of kernel cost: 5.0s to import Mathlib against 0.1s for a three-obligation proof, measured over three runs each. Reuse would be worth roughly 50x on a repair loop.
prefix_reuse.why_not_built: The available REPL returned success-shaped output while running against an empty environment — `Unknown identifier trivial` after a reported successful import. A fast path that succeeds emptily is worse than no fast path. See doctrine/kernel_economics.md.
prefix_reuse.gate_before_enabling: any fast path must reproduce the slow path's verdict on every artifact in scripts/negative_control/, rejections and acceptance alike — a backend that has lost its environment passes nothing and fails nothing, and only a set of inputs whose verdicts should differ exposes it

tiers.name: bounded
tiers.description: Exhaustive or randomized search over a stated finite domain — one integer variable or a product of several, so pair and triple questions are expressible — dispatched to scripts/backends/ (SAT with witness re-verification and labelled refutations; exact arithmetic; finite enumeration). Adversarial within its range and establishes nothing outside it — a budget stop is UNKNOWN, never a refutation.
tiers.two_sided_evidence: scripts/negative_control/ holds two known-FALSE claims the tier must refute: bounded_false_claim.json (n^2 > n, false at n = 0 and n = 1) and bounded_false_pair.json (C(n,k) >= n, false at k = 0, and inexpressible without the second search axis). scripts/check.py --self-test runs both. A search backend that returns 'no counterexample' for the wrong reason is indistinguishable from a working one on inputs where the answer is yes, so the controls are inputs where it is no.
tiers.contamination_controls: Bounds and seed are frozen in the claim before the search runs, so a failing search cannot be rescued by quietly shrinking the range.

receipt_format.freshness_rule: The receipt records the artifact SHA-256 at elaboration time and the toolchain identity. It is stale if either differs from the live artifact and current toolchain at the exit gate, which recomputes both rather than trusting the recorded values. A passing build from an earlier edit is the standard way a broken artifact launders itself, so a receipt whose timestamp precedes the artifact's last modification is rejected outright.

escalation.failure_signature: The pair (failure_class, normalized first diagnostic line with file positions, identifier suffixes, and metavariable numbers stripped). Two failures with the same pair are the same failure; a repeat escalates immediately rather than waiting out the count, because the second attempt evidently changed nothing the checker could see.

rules.why: read AFTER a failure: diagnosing into a class is what makes the next attempt different
the frozen statement is what everything downstream is checked against
how a long campaign is run
the plan a candidate is rendered from
the last thing before a status moves
what is already known, before anything is attempted
when a status has to come down
moving work out of the open core
what may and may not be called solved

refute_attempt.name: kernel-recheck
refute_attempt.description: Re-elaborate the artifact from its current bytes in a fresh process against a fresh checkout, then audit the axioms the result actually depends on. Because the kernel cannot be talked into a false pass, surviving this is a genuine attempt to break the result rather than a second friendly run.

additional.name: placeholder-scan
additional.description: Rejects sorry, admit, axiom, constant, opaque, unsafe, native_decide, and the `?_`/`by?` holes. These make anything type-check, so their presence voids the kernel's verdict entirely.

additional.name: target-protection-diff
additional.description: Diffs the artifact's statement against the frozen target: signature, binders, hypotheses, domains, and definitions. Catches the target being weakened to something trivially true, an assumption being smuggled into a binder, or a definition being redefined to make the claim vacuous.

additional.name: axiom-audit
additional.description: Enumerates the axioms the checked result depends on and rejects any beyond the declared allowlist. A new or metaprogrammed axiom is an escape hatch that a plain type-check will not surface.

additional.name: circularity-audit
additional.description: Renders the proof term and refuses it if it cites the target itself, or any library declaration of the same type. The kernel accepts `theorem t : P := library_t`, `#print axioms` reports it clean, and every other gate passes it — so on any target the library already contains, this is the only thing standing between a search and its own answer key.

additional.name: premise-precondition-audit
additional.description: Every cited external result has its hypotheses matched against the local use. A citation whose preconditions are unmet is an unresolved gap, not a step. Reads the plan's declared citations, so it applies to the WIT artifact; on a checked artifact it audited zero citations and passed, which is not a check. What a tactic reaches for in a checked artifact is the circularity audit's question.

additional.name: fidelity-review
additional.description: Independent bidirectional check that the formal statement says what the informal target says. The kernel proves things about the encoding; whether the encoding is faithful is a separate question it cannot answer.

VERIFIED_WIT.description: Structurally valid WIT with every obligation carrying an accepted verdict. Says nothing about semantic truth — the structural tier's ceiling is SKETCH, so this refinement is reachable only alongside a kernel receipt.

VERIFIED_LEAN.description: Kernel-checked against Mathlib with a fresh hash-bound receipt, a clean axiom audit, and a passing fidelity review.

CHECKED_SYMBOLIC.description: Established by exact symbolic computation over a stated domain rather than by enumeration.

reference_data.purpose: The method families an approach can belong to. Two arguments differing only in manipulation are one family, and the count is what decides whether a target is genuinely stuck.
The mutations available when an approach stalls: what to change about a target that is not the target itself.
